extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, businesses, stakeholders, and government respondents invited to submit comments on federal information-collection notices (PRA notices) and to respond to agency qualitative feedback instruments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for submitting public comments on federal information-collection notices (Paperwork Reduction Act notices) and for agency collections of qualitative feedback (generic clearances). Covers what commenters should address, procedural submission rules, privacy cautions, and conditions under which agencies may use generic clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record and personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, all comments received will become public records, including any personal information provided. Sensitive personal information, such as account numbers or Social Security numbers, should not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments submitted in response to notices will be part of the public record. Do not include sensitive personal information (examples given: account numbers, Social Security numbers). Agencies reiterate this across notices and warn submitters not to provide PII in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comments — Necessity and Practical Utility
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the [agency], including whether the information will have practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies invite commenters to evaluate whether the proposed information collection is needed to perform the agency’s functions and whether the information will be practically useful to those functions (e.g., program management, service delivery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comments — Accuracy of Burden Estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) The accuracy of the [agency]’s estimate of the burden of the collection of information, including the validity of the methods and the assumptions used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should assess the reasonableness of the agency’s estimates (number of respondents, total burden hours, average burden per response) and the methods/assumptions used to produce those estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comments — Enhance Quality, Utility, and Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies solicit concrete suggestions to improve survey instruments, forms, questions, and instructions so the information collected will be clearer, more useful, and higher quality (e.g., question wording changes, format changes, examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comments — Minimize Respondent Burden
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) Ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on respondents, including through the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should propose methods to reduce time/cost to respondents, such as electronic submission options, streamlined questions, pre-filled data, or other automation. Agencies note that comments will be summarized and/or included in requests to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and deadline for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments are encouraged and must be received on or before [specified deadline] to be assured of consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each notice specifies a cut-off date (e.g., June 23, July 21). Comments received after the comment period will generally not be accepted. Submit on or before the stated date to ensure consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and docket identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments and recommendations should be sent within 30 days of publication of this notice to www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain or via the Federal eRulemaking Portal (www.regulations.gov); email submissions should include the docket number in the subject line; paper mail/hand delivery is accepted but electronic submission is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the notice-specific instructions: include agency name, agency form number or OMB number, and docket number; electronic submissions are preferred due to potential mail delays. Some notices list multiple acceptable channels (regs.gov, specified email address, mail/hand delivery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit comments to certain email boxes / alternative contact instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: If alternative electronic format or further information is requested, contact specified accessibility or PRA officer emails, but: Please do not submit comments to these email boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices provide contact emails (e.g., CFPB_PRA@cfpb.gov, CFPB_Accessibility@cfpb.gov) for information requests or alternative formats but explicitly instruct submitters not to file comments to those addresses. Use the methods specified in the ADDRESSES section for comment submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of qualitative feedback (generic clearance)
rubrics_metrics.description: By qualitative feedback, the agency means information that provides useful insights on, for example, comprehension, usability, perceptions, and opinions, but are not statistical surveys that yield quantitative results that can be generalized to the population of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative feedback is suitable for understanding user perceptions, identifying issues, and informing service delivery improvements; it is not intended for producing statistically generalizable results or monitoring trends over time without more rigorous designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for use of generic clearance for qualitative collections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency will only submit a collection for approval under this generic clearance if it meets the following conditions:

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback target areas for service-delivery collections
rubrics_metrics.description: The solicitation of feedback will target areas such as: timeliness, appropriateness, accuracy of information, courtesy, efficiency of service delivery, and resolution of issues with service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies will assess responses across these dimensions to plan and inform efforts to improve or maintain service quality. Collections should be tailored to gather perceptions and experiences relevant to these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information necessary to validate trustworthiness for system access (DD Form 2875)
rubrics_metrics.description: The information collection is necessary for validating the trustworthiness of individuals who request access to DoD systems and information. When an individual requires access to a DoD information system, application, or database, he/she retrieves the DD Form 2875. The requestor’s security requirements (background investigation and clearance information) are identified on the DD Form 2875 and validated by the cognizant Security Manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collection ensures system access granted is consistent with national security interests; references Executive Order 10450 and instructs that details be validated by Security Managers. This describes the substantive need/standard for collecting personnel security information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and procedures for DD Forms 2065 and 1375 (Disposition of Remains; reimbursement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DD Form 2065 records the sponsor’s disposition instructions for the remains and associated costs; the DD Form 1375 is used to request payment of interment allowance. The sponsor must complete and sign the forms; the CAO will aid completion and return the completed form to the Service Casualty Office (SCO); claims must include supporting documents (e.g., receipts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirements: forms accompany remains, must be signed by sponsor/claimant, include receipts for services, are uploaded to Defense Casualty Information Processing System (DCIPS), and include Privacy Act statements to notify respondents of disclosures. Claims are adjudicated by the Military Service and payments processed accordingly.
